items.summary: Droughts, floods and extreme heat are upping the pressure on delegates at the UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. Can countries move beyond pledges to concrete action?

items.title: Poland: Gunman kills 6 in Krakow main square
items.summary: A gunman who fired from a car killed at least six people, including a British tourist, in Krakow's main market square. Officials said the shooter was fascinated with "radical" and "far-right" ideologies.

items.title: Ebola: Why is there still no vaccine?
items.summary: Ebola has been known about for decades, but there is still no vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of the virus causing the current outbreak. New research raises hopes of protection against the various types of Ebola.

items.summary: President Isaac Herzog has picked former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, leader of an anti-Netanyahu alliance, to take the first shot at trying to form a government, with tricky coalition talks expected.

items.summary: US President Donald Trump has offered the White House press secretary job to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship. White has neither formally accepted nor turned down the invitation.

items.title: France sees new round of Yellow Vest, student protests
items.summary: Although fewer protesters turned out in comparison with previous weeks, several cities saw clashes between police and demonstrators.

items.title: Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?
items.summary: While Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Could the EU's pragmatic stance risk repeating past mistakes?

items.title: South Africa's ANC facing worst-ever performance in local elections
items.summary: Near-final results show South Africa's once dominant ANC will see its lowest-ever vote percentage. The party is taking the blame for shoddy municipal services, including water and electricity shortages.

items.title: More than 40,000 gather as Pope Leo XIV celebrates Mass in Uruguay
items.summary: Leo celebrated the first Mass of his South America tour less than a month after undergoing cancer surgery. He is seeking to raise interest in the Catholic Church in Uruguay, South America's most secular country.

items.title: Journalism and AI: Who owns the news?
items.summary: Publishers say AI chatbots are using their reporting to answer readers' questions while sending back less traffic and less money. Should the companies that build these tools pay for the journalism they rely on?

items.title: Son of Iran's shah receives 'Freedom Prize' in Frankfurt
items.summary: 18,000 people gathered in Frankfurt to show support for Reza Pahlavi, the son of the Iranian monarch ousted in 1979. Factions in the opposition have accused him of not distancing himself from his father's rule.

items.title: After victory in the midterms, what next for US Democrats?
items.summary: Donald Trump's Republican party has lost its majority in both chambers of the US Congress. But the president still has a lot of power — and the Democrats have yet to agree on how best to use theirs.

items.title: Italy's Meloni blames pro-Russian hackers for cyberattack on minister
items.summary: Antonio Tajani has said hackers published personal data stolen from him as Giorgia Meloni blamed pro-Russia criminals for the incident. The news follows a string of bomb threats that have grounded flights across the EU.

items.title: Yemen: 22 killed in strike near Sanaa, Houthis say
items.summary: The Iran-backed Houthi rebel group accused Saudi Arabia of hitting several homes in the village of al-Shariya near the Yemeni capital. There was no initial comment from Riyadh.

items.title: New Zealand election too close to call with over 95% of votes counted
items.summary: Initial results in New Zealand show the two main parties neck-and-neck with fewer than 4,000 votes separating them. Official results aren't expected until later this month once special votes have been counted.

items.title: Germany hopes to host world ice hockey championship — without Russia
items.summary: International protests continue after a court ruled that Russia must be allowed to return to international ice hockey. Germany is seeking a solution that will allow the country to host next year's world championship.

items.title: Ukraine: Russia hits Kyiv with airstrikes ahead of trilateral talks
items.summary: The strikes hit a major bridge and energy facilities in the Kyiv region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Moscow of trying to "push" Ukraine "into a blackout" ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi.

items.title: Germany news: Son of Iran's last shah takes center stage in Frankfurt

items.title: Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck

items.summary: Czech arms makers have thrived on demand linked to the war in Ukraine. To sustain their growth, they need to look beyond ammunition and toward new technologies — and even space.

items.summary: As ice hockey's governing body continues to wrangle over how to respond to a CAS order to reinstate Russia to international play, the top women's tournament gets underway in Denmark without Russia.

items.summary: European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets.

items.summary: DW has found that three-quarters of Russia's weightlifting team had no independent out-of-competition testing before this year's world championships, despite the country's doping history.

items.title: Pioneering Jewish academy opens in Germany
items.summary: A Jewish academy has opened its doors in Frankfurt. The Central Council of Jews in Germany, the country’s leading Jewish umbrella group, set up the project to combat hate and promote dialogue and learning nationally.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
items.summary: The announcement by the footballing legend comes just weeks after a public spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.

items.title: 36 years later: Hungary opens Communist-era secret service files
items.summary: Decades after the end of Soviet rule, Hungary is releasing all its secret service files. The disclosure is sparking fresh debate about informants, guilt and responsibility.

items.summary: The Republic of Cyprus long balanced ties between Russia and the West. Now, it is phasing out Russian weapons, expanding defense cooperation with the United States and redefining its place in the Eastern Mediterranean.

items.title: Multiple flights to European airports targeted by bomb threats

items.title: How Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria

items.summary: German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.

items.title: IIHF ordered to allow Russia back into world championships

items.title: Germany's Alexander Zverev clinches tennis No. 1 ranking

items.summary: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.

items.summary: The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.
